item.title: Re: Am I A Bad Person?
item.content:encoded:
How does the Foundation fit into this story? What does this look like as an article?

Keep in mind that part of the challenge is figuring out how to present these stories. As it stands right now, you've got a couple distinct problems. How on earth does the serial killer find out about the rich family's ability? How does the Foundation know?

Same questions about how the Foundation knows about the serial killer or the diary - which feels like a rather convenient macguffin through which to tell the story.

Why would the Foundation care about a random dead corpse with a book full of crazy ranting?

You've got a lot of information that would be difficult to impossible for the Foundation to reasonably know, but you've not told us how any of this comes to be known or how it will be presented. I'm not even sure what the description of this would look like.

item.title: Re: Am I A Bad Person?
item.content:encoded:
Holy crap, I absolutely freakin' love this idea.

And now I must explain why I cannot grant you a Greenlight just yet.

+Let us start the crit!
-Let's do it!

Now, my thought process is very…how should I say it…fast and slow at the same time, so please forgive me if I ramble a bit.

Before we begin, I have to say this: the way you wrote this in your concept pitch was kinda awkward to pick through. You put part of the story with the Elevator Pitch, part of the story in the Central Narrative, and the rest in the Hook/Attention-Grabber and Additional Notes. But I won't bug you too much with that.

So first, let's start with the Elevator Pitch. I really dig it. It's an object that grants wish fulfilment-based superpowers. It's simple, but the possibilities are absolutely endless. You could write anything with this. Literally anything.

That said, the Central Narrative.

I really like it for the most part, but I spotted some weirdnesses (sorry, my vocabulary today is a little off) that I'd like to address.

The story is narrated by the author of the diary: a serial killer who spared the life of the overwhelmingly attractive man.

So…the serial killer was the author of the diary? As in he wrote it originally? And then the doctors had it for some reason and then the serial killer got it back?

The superpower had then passed on to the serial killer, even tho they had no blood connection.

So, does he end up getting the diary back or no? Or is the superpower just passed to him next because he was the original owner?

The serial killer gained the ability to "read" a person's entire life by looking at their face, as well as being able to predict all outcomes of any interaction he exerts with them, which informs perfect place, time and method to kill them without a trace.

This is the part that caught me. This is horrifying. Not to mention, instead of just having Evil Murder McBadPerson, you decided to make him have internal turmoil with his own humanity. That said, gonna have to figure how to make that bit work without having it feel forced.

He stopped the murders and dedicated the last days of life trying to seal his powers within the diary's last page by using his blood

Is this… actually how the thing works or is the serial killer just delusional?

he believed in the existence of an afterlife in which he could continue to use these powers

So he wants to keep killing in an afterlife where everyone's already dead? This bit's a headscratcher and a half…

He could escape the Foundation.

Tbh considering he can just use his predictive outcome powers to get away with anything, he could just get away from the Foundation whenever he wished. Unless it was purely the moral problem that was eating away at him.

I do wanna know how he ended up gaining empathy after gaining these powers anyways.

Did he end up seeing that many people's lifetimes that he realized the magnitude of taking human life?

Feel free to PM me once you cleared up all of these.

I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day, partner!

👍

EDIT:

So, I was PMed with more information on this idea and I do still think it has a lot of promise, but after I read Riemann's crit on this, I feel kinda silly not thinking of those issues earlier.

In terms of light status, it is not quite green, not yet. I'd say you're sitting at a steady yellow right now. My sides of the issue are fixed, I'd say. I just ask that you add everything I read in your PM into your concept post and make it neater to read, then follow up on Riemann 's crit.

I think I've done all I can now. Good luck with your idea, mate!

item.title: Am I A Bad Person?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: A serial killer with mind-reading abilities, able to predict all outcomes of an interaction he engages with someone, as well as the easiest and quickest ways to achieve them. He can also read an individual's entire life by reaching to their memories, obtaining enough information to lure them in any way. He had a simple life as a photographer, which allowed him to find victims more easily by taking photos of frequently visited places. Because of his superpowers, he always knew the perfect place, time and method to kill his victims without a trace.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The serial killer surrendered to a Foundation intelligence agency shortly after killing two of their agents who were working on the investigation of a series of disappearances in a specific region of the US, which he claimed to be responsible for. He demonstrates how his powers work live to the agents during a brief interrogation, confirming the existence of an anomaly case. However, even without posing any threat, because he proved to be responsible for a series of crimes that could otherwise lead to a severe court sentence, he was escorted to the Foundation by an MTF squad. He constantly offers himself to help the Foundation with several tasks, such as in investigative processes, containment of anomalies, and even janitorial work, trying to get the Foundation to grant all of his "requests for individual rights" (most of which, if not all, are denied).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He tells Foundation personnel that, upon a period of usage of his powers, he had developed a side effect: When accessing an individual's memory, he will quickly experience the feelings present in those memories so vividly that he can even feel their pain. This restricted him from killing by slowly bringing the desire to empathize with his victims, causing him to conflict with his own moral values. Because of that, when he discovered the Foundation through the memories of a field agent who he happened to pass by, he decided to change his killing methods in order to lure the Foundation's eyes. He surrendered to them on purpose, just so he would not need to use his powers constantly to evade authorities, thus giving him time to regain his composure. It remains to be seen his other intentions within the Foundation.

Additional Notes: I really don't know if calling an MTF squad for containment would really be necessary, considering that the level of threat was not fully known. Perhaps yes for he being a serial killer? Because he has already proven that he can do whatever goes on in his head without being stopped.
